why.numbers_show_results.i2_title: Wrong moves are a separate results item (decision «Числа — Результаты»): v1 hid them inside «Level points». Items: level points (@DIST = removed digits × points_good_move), wrong moves (@P1 × @P2 = W × points_wrong_move), time penalty (@TIME × @P3 = seconds × time_penalty). The total is unchanged.
why.numbers_show_results.i3_points_arr: @P3 = time_penalty_arr (or sp_time_penalty_arr in the test) of the running game, so the item always matches the price used.
why.numbers_sp_show_results.i2_title: Same three items in the test; the prices come from the sp_* keys (BUG-NUM-02).
why.MG_numbers_easy.in_app_ver_level_up_para: 3.7 (owner: the Numbers threshold became too low): up 2500 = T ≤ 85 s without wrong moves on the 15-digit field (3.6 had 2000 = 95 s, 3.3 had 3000 = 75 s; one wrong move = 9 s). Novice 56 %, average 95 %, strong 100 % of games; the novice passes Easy in 5 games (median). The model novice of Numbers is twice as slow as the average player and often ends at 0, so a threshold fitted to the 3.6 Easy target (novice 60–75 %) asks almost nothing of everyone else. The prices are unchanged (−50 per second on Easy, see numbers_game_field.time_penalty_arr).
why.MG_numbers_easy.level_up_param: Same threshold as in_app_ver_level_up_param (that one is read first); unlock 3 kept.
why.numbers_game_field.time_penalty_arr: Hard −40 per second (original −60; −30 since 3.2 for the 49-digit field). On the 35-digit field the average player needs 153 s: at −60 time would take 44 % of the maximum and the novice (292 s) would end most games at 0; at −40 time takes 29 % and wrong moves 10 %, and the mean rises on every step: novice 2034 / 3136 / 5997, average 4005 / 7277 / 12816 (Hard = 1.76 × Medium), strong 5440 / 10633 / 17699. A Hard game without wrong moves beats the average player's typical Medium game up to 343 s, 2.2 × his usual time. Easy and Medium stay −60; the test reads sp_time_penalty_arr. Easy −60 → −50 per second: On Easy the novice (79 s, 1 wrong move) ends 21 % of games with 0 points. With −50 per second on Easy he ends 12 % at 0; means novice 2590 / 3136 / 5997 still rise (−40 would put his Easy mean above his Medium mean). up 3000 then gives novice 46 %, average 90 %.
why.numbers_game_field.points_wrong_move_arr: Value unchanged (Hard −1000 since 3.2, original −2000; Easy −450, Medium −1000). On the 35-digit Hard field the average player makes 2.1 wrong moves, 10 % of the 21000 maximum (Medium: 1.0 = 8 %). The results window takes the running prices (@P2, @P3); the test reads sp_points_wrong_move_arr.
why.MG_numbers_hard.level_up_param: up stays 15000, now for the 35-digit field at 600 per digit and −40 per second (without wrong moves T ≤ 150 s; the average player needs 153 s and makes 2.1 wrong moves of 25 s each). Average 9 → 25 % of games (target 20–30 %; median 114 → 39 games for the 10 steps), novice 1 %, strong 91 → 97 % (target 75–90 % is not reachable together with the average's: the strong player is twice as fast; 16000 gives strong 91 % and average 13 %). Games under down (6000): average 3 %, novice 49 %.
why.shell.b_mark_pnt_tables.108: Numbers Medium with the test base of 650 per digit. The current table is flat in the middle and strict at the top (100 % needs ≤ 11 s for the whole field): 22 / 50 / 73 / 84, and 25 % of novice attempts end at raw 0. New marks: 25 / 50 / 80 / 93.
why.numbers_game_field.sp_points_good_move_a: Test-only key. 650 instead of 530 per removed digit raises the base from 13 250 to 16 250, so novices no longer clamp at raw 0 (25 % → 8 % of novice attempts). The prices of a mistake (−1000) and of a second (−60) stay: a cheaper mistake would make placing the number into a guessed cell attractive.
why.rules.numbers.fields: Playable rectangle, columns × rows, per difficulty; the digits fill it without its outer ring: 15 / 25 / 35 digits. Hard was 9×9 with 49 digits: 18.6 moves instead of the 10.3 of Medium, each over more cells (13.9 checks against 8.6), so the average player's Hard game took 241 s against 84 s on Medium (2.9 ×) with 3.2 wrong moves against 1.0, and the novice's 7.7 minutes — a cliff, not a step. With 9×7: 13.5 moves, 153 s (1.8 × Medium; Medium is 2.0 × Easy), 2.1 wrong moves. The Hard task rule stays (cells with at least 3 neighbours, frequent digits dropped). Easy and Medium, the test field, are unchanged. Search model of tools/analysis/train_balance_numbers.mjs on the real createField / chooseDigit / acceptMove, calibrated on the Medium field to 15 / 8 / 4 s per move and 2 / 1 / 0.2 wrong moves. Needs the code change (the margins are constants of numbers-model.js); without it use if_no_code_change.
why.numbers_game_field.points_good_move_arr: Hard: 600 per removed digit (was 430, less than the 530 of Medium). 35 digits × 600 = 21000, the same maximum as 49 × 430. Easy 450 and Medium 530 are unchanged; the test reads sp_points_good_move_arr.
why.MG_numbers_med.level_up_param: 3.7 (owner: the Numbers threshold became too low): up 5500 = T ≤ 129 s without wrong moves on the 25-digit field, 112 s with one (3.6 had 4000 = 154 s, 3.3 had 7200 = 100 s; the average player needs 81 s and makes one wrong move = 16.7 s). Novice 24 %, average 79 %, strong 100 %; games for the 5 steps (median): novice 20, average 6. Games under down (2200): average 3 %, novice 44 %. Between the 3.3 and the 3.6 values on purpose: the 3.6 target (novice 35–45 %) gave 4000, which a player of average speed passes with any game he finishes.
